photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: Studio portrait of two named Assiniboine individuals in traditional dress—quilled/beaded bandolier bag, fringed hide dress, trade cloth shawl, and moccasins—documentary photo of their attire fits the claimed ethnicity.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: A documentary group photograph of Assiniboine men and a child in traditional dress and ornament, standing before tepees with a horse in the background—a straightforward ethnographic photo of the people's dress and daily life.

photo.name: postcard; photographic print
photo.title: postcard (colour tinted ('photochrom')); photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: Studio/documentary postcard portrait of Irene Rock, identified as Assiniboine, in beaded dress with chest ornament, beside a tipi and saddled horse with beaded saddle blanket — clear documentary photo of dress and material culture.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: Full-length studio portrait of Black Raven, identified as an Assiniboine man, wearing a wool/hide coat, hair and neck ornaments, studded belt with knife sheath, and footwear — a documentary photo of the dress of the claimed people.

photo.name: postcard; photographic print
photo.title: postcard (colour tinted ('photochrom')); photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: A colorized photo postcard of George Rustler, identified as an Assiniboine man, mounted on horseback in decorated fringed hide tunic, leggings, and moccasins — a documentary photo of dress consistent with the claimed people.

photo.name: postcard; photographic print
photo.title: postcard (colour tinted ('photochrom')); photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: A photochrom postcard portrait of "Rattlesnake," an Assiniboine man, mounted on a horse in hide tunic, blanket, leggings, feathers, and holding a gun — a documentary photo of dress and daily life matching the claimed people.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: Studio portrait of an identified Assiniboine man, Big Elk, wearing traditional hair style, neck ornament, wool coat and belted knife sheath — documentary dress photo fitting the claimed people.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: Studio portrait of Jumping Sheep, identified as an Assiniboine man, wearing a wool/fur-trimmed coat, studded belt, and cartridge belt with knife sheath — documentary dress photo clearly consistent with the claimed people.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: Full-length studio portrait of "Muddy," an Assiniboine man, wearing a wool coat/blanket garment, belt with sheathed knife, and footwear — a documentary photo of dress belonging to the named culture.

photo.name: stereoscope photograph
photo.title: stereoscope photograph (black and white)
photo.reason: A documentary stereoview of a Native encampment with tipis, lodges and horses at Fort Union, a major historic trading post on the Assiniboine's home range along the upper Missouri, consistent with the claimed people's daily/trading life.

arms.name: Club
arms.title: Club (skullcracker)
arms.reason: A stone-headed war club with carved/painted human-face head on a beaded, quilled, and feather-trimmed wooden handle, consistent with Plains/Assiniboine "skullcracker" clubs used as weapons.

garment.name: Tobacco bag
garment.title: Tobacco Bag
garment.reason: This is a beaded and quilled hide tobacco bag with long fringe, a classic Plains item used and made by Assiniboine people; though the museum calls it "textile," it is actually a hide garment/bag accessory.
